cards.front: Suelo ir al gimnasio dos veces a la semana.
cards.back: I usually go to the gym twice a week.

cards.front: Mi novio suele correr tres veces a la semana.
cards.back: My boyfriend usually goes running three times a week.

cards.front: Mi madre suele salir a andar una vez al mes.
cards.back: My mother usually goes walking once a month.

cards.front: Antes yo iba al gimnasio tres veces a la semana.
cards.back: I used to go to the gym three times a week.

cards.front: Mi novio antes corría cinco veces a la semana.
cards.back: My boyfriend used to go running five times a week.

cards.front: Mi madre solía salir a pasear una vez a la semana.
cards.back: My mother used to go walking once a week.

cards.front: Suelo ir al gimnasio dos veces a la semana, pero solía ir tres veces a la semana.
cards.back: I usually go to the gym twice a week, but I used to go three times a week.

cards.front: Mi novio suele ir a correr cuatro veces a la semana, pero solía ir cinco veces a la semana.
cards.back: My boyfriend usually goes running four times a week, but he used to go five times a week.

cards.front: Mi madre suele salir a caminar una vez al mes, pero antes solía ir dos veces a la semana.
cards.back: My mother usually goes walking once a month, but she used to go twice a week.

cards.front: Antes yo estaba más en forma.
cards.back: I used to be fitter.

cards.front: Mi novio antes estaba más en forma.
cards.back: My boyfriend used to be in better shape.

cards.front: Mi madre antes estaba más sana.
cards.back: My mother used to be healthier.

cards.front: Antes era entrenador personal, pero ya no lo soy.
cards.back: I used to be a fitness instructor but I'm not any more.

cards.front: Mi novio antes salía a correr cinco veces a la semana. Ya no lo hace.
cards.back: My boyfriend used to go running five times a week. He doesn't any more.

cards.front: Mi madre antes salía a caminar dos veces a la semana. Ya no lo hace.
cards.back: My mother used to go walking twice a week. She doesn't any more.

cards.front: ¿Sueles salir los sábados?
cards.back: Do you usually go out on Saturdays?

cards.front: ¿Tu madre suele tomar té los domingos?
cards.back: Does your mother usually have tea on Sundays?

cards.front: ¿Tu departamento suele salir a comer los viernes?
cards.back: Does your department usually go out for lunch on Fridays?

cards.front: ¿Solías salir los sábados antes de tener tu bebé?
cards.back: Did you use to go out on Saturdays before you had a baby?

cards.front: ¿Tu madre solía tomar té los domingos antes de mudarse a España?
cards.back: Did your mother use to have tea on Sundays before she moved to Spain?

cards.front: ¿Tu departamento solía comer fuera los viernes antes de que el nuevo jefe empezara?
cards.back: Did your department use to go out for lunch on Fridays before the new boss started?

cards.front: No solía salir los sábados incluso antes de tener un bebé.
cards.back: I didn't use to go out on Saturdays, even before I had a baby.

cards.front: Mi madre no solía tomar té los domingos incluso antes de mudarse a España.
cards.back: My mother didn't use to have tea on Sundays, even before she moved to Spain.

cards.front: Nuestro departamento no solía comer fuera incluso antes de que llegara el nuevo jefe.
cards.back: Our department didn't use to go out for lunch, even before the new boss started.

cards.front: Hoy en día la gente no suele escribir cartas, pero antes sí lo hacía.
cards.back: Nowadays, people don't usually write letters, but they used to.

cards.front: Hoy en día la gente no suele comprar el periódico, pero antes sí lo hacía.
cards.back: Nowadays, people don't usually buy the newspaper, but they used to.

cards.front: Hoy en día la gente no suele llevar pelucas, pero antes sí lo hacía.
cards.back: Nowadays, people don't usually wear wigs, but they used to.

cards.front: No solía cocinar los fines de semana, pero ahora sí lo hago.
cards.back: I didn't use to cook at the weekend, but I usually do now.

cards.front: No solía llevar corbata, pero ahora sí suelo llevar.
cards.back: I didn't use to wear a tie, but I usually do now.

cards.front: No solía llevar maquillaje, pero ahora sí suelo llevar.
cards.back: I didn't use to wear makeup, but I usually do now.

cards.front: Estoy acostumbrada al mal tiempo en Inglaterra.
cards.back: I'm used to the bad weather in England.

cards.front: ¿Está acostumbrada Clara al mal tiempo en Inglaterra?
cards.back: Is Clara used to the bad weather in England?

cards.front: No, no está acostumbrada a ello todavía.
cards.back: No, she isn't used to it yet.

cards.front: Clara no puede acostumbrarse a la comida inglesa.
cards.back: Clara can't get used to English food.

cards.front: ¿Crees que se acostumbrará algún día?
cards.back: Do you think she'll ever get used to it?

cards.front: Creo que nunca se acostumbrará.
cards.back: I don't think she'll ever get used to it.

cards.front: ¿Clara está acostumbrada a conducir por la izquierda?
cards.back: Is Clara used to driving on the left-hand side?

cards.front: Sí, ya está acostumbrada a conducir por la izquierda.
cards.back: Yes, she's already used to driving on the left-hand side.

cards.front: ¿Está acostumbrada a ponerse el impermeable todos los días?
cards.back: Is she used to wearing a raincoat every day?

cards.front: ¿Clara se está acostumbrando a vivir en Inglaterra?
cards.back: Is Clara getting used to living in England?

cards.front: Claro que sí, se está acostumbrando a ello.
cards.back: Of course, she's getting used to it.

cards.front: Se está acostumbrando a hablar en inglés todos los días.
cards.back: She's getting used to speaking English every day.

cards.front: ¿Cuesta mucho acostumbrarse a vivir en Inglaterra?
cards.back: Does living in England take much getting-used-to?

cards.front: Sí, cuesta bastante acostumbrarse a vivir en Inglaterra.
cards.back: Yes, living in England takes some getting-used-to.

cards.front: No cuesta mucho acostumbrarse a conducir por la izquierda.
cards.back: Driving on the left-hand side doesn't take much getting-used-to.

cards.back: It's no use complaining. Get over it!

cards.back: It's no use crying over spilt milk. Get over it!

cards.front: ¿De qué sirve discutir por cosas pequeñas?
cards.back: What's the use in arguing about small things?

cards.front: ¿De qué sirve quejarse? ¡Olvídalo!
cards.back: What's the use in complaining? Get over it!

cards.front: ¡De qué sirve!
cards.back: What's the use!

cards.back: What's the point in telling him the truth?

cards.front: ¿De qué sirve fingir que nunca ocurrió?
cards.back: What's the point in pretending it never happened?

cards.front: ¿De qué sirve tratar de convencerle?
cards.back: What's the point in trying to convince him?

cards.front: ¡A lo hecho, pecho!
cards.back: There's no point in crying over spilt milk.

cards.front: No sirve de nada negarlo.
cards.back: There's no point in denying it.

cards.front: Es inútil fingir que nunca ocurrió. ¡Olvídalo!
cards.back: There's no point in pretending it never happened. Get over it!

cards.front: ¿Sirve de algo quejarse por ello?
cards.back: Is there any point in complaining about it?

cards.front: ¿Sirve de algo llamarle?
cards.back: Is there any point in calling him?

cards.back: Do you think there's any point in waiting for him?

cards.back: Energy use is really high in the US.

cards.back: The US government is promoting clean energy use.

cards.back: Does water use go up in the winter?

cards.back: Does water use go down in the summer?

cards.front: El consumo de agua descendió debido a la sequía.
cards.back: Water use went down because of the drought.

cards.front: El consumo de drogas es un problema aún más serio en los barrios urbanos que en las afueras.
cards.back: Drug use is more of a serious problem in the inner cities than in the suburbs.

cards.front: Esa fotocopiadora es de uso público.
cards.back: That photocopier is for public use.

cards.front: ¿Sabes si la piscina es de uso público?
cards.back: Do you know if the swimming pool is for public use?

cards.back: I think the photocopier is for public use but I don't think the swimming pool is for public use.

cards.front: Esa piscina es solo de uso privado.
cards.back: That swimming pool is for private use only.

cards.front: Esa fotocopiadora es solo de uso privado.
cards.back: That photocopier is for private use only.

cards.front: No sé si la impresora es de uso privado o de uso público.
cards.back: I don't know if the printer is for private use or for public use.

cards.front: Una linterna es útil cuando te vas de camping.
cards.back: A torch is useful when you go camping.

cards.front: Unos tacones no son muy útiles cuando te vas de camping.
cards.back: High heels aren't very useful when you go camping.

cards.front: ¿Por qué unos tacones no son útiles cuando te vas de camping?
cards.back: Why aren't high heels useful when you go camping?

cards.back: That underground map you gave me was very handy.

cards.front: Ese mapa callejero que me dio la Oficina de Turismo me resultó muy útil.
cards.back: The street map Tourist Information gave me came in very handy.

cards.front: La guía de Madrid que me dieron mis padres por Navidad me resultó útil.
cards.back: The Madrid guide my parents gave me for Christmas came in handy.

cards.front: Los tacones altos son completamente inútiles para irse de camping.
cards.back: High heels are completely useless for camping.

cards.front: Ese mapa del metro que me diste es totalmente inútil.
cards.back: That underground map you gave me is totally useless.

cards.back: I forgot to get him a birthday present. I'm useless!

cards.back: Our team was hopeless. We lost by three goals.

cards.back: The interview was hopeless. I didn't get the job.

cards.back: It was a hopeless situation. They didn't survive.

cards.back: Wearing high heels when you go camping is pointless.

cards.back: Pretending it never happened is pointless.

cards.front: Intentar convencerle a él no tiene sentido.
cards.back: Trying to convince him is pointless.
